Sam (support): Marcus — opening thread here based on the ticket. You mentioned mTLS verify_timeouts to the Private control plane after egress firewall changes. Can you paste the failing client logs / openssl output and any tcpdump you have?

Marcus (Customer): Repro steps from our bastion inside the VPC:
`openssl s_client -connect cp.prod.redwood.example:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile ca.pem -msg -debug`
Output (trimmed):
```
>>> TLS 1.2 Handshake [length 0091]
    ClientHello, TLSv1.2
[...lots of ClientHello bytes...]
read:errno=104
140735219527616:error:140770FC:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol:s23_clnt.c:782:
---
no peer certificate available
---
Verify return code: 0 (ok)
```
And our agent logs show repeated `tls: handshake did not complete` and then an application-level timeout. This started right after we tightened outbound rules and enabled "drop fragmented packets" on the egress firewall.

Ingrid (SRE): Thanks. Two quick asks: 1) can you share a short tcpdump capture (pcap) of the handshake attempt? 2) can you also run `openssl s_client -connect cp.prod.redwood.example:443 -msg` without certs to see raw TLS messages? The symptoms (ClientHello sent, no ServerHello / read errno) often point to a middlebox dropping fragments or trimming TLS extensions.

oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1780456789 (support escalation)

Marcus (Customer): Uploading tcpdump excerpt. Key lines (client IP 10.10.5.21 -> cp IP 3.120.45.9):
```
12:01:05.123456 IP 10.10.5.21.52344 > 3.120.45.9.443: Flags [P.], seq 1:1461, ack 1, win 64240, length 1460
12:01:05.123460 IP 10.10.5.21.52344 > 3.120.45.9.443: Flags [P.], seq 1461:2921, ack 1, win 64240, length 1460
12:01:05.124100 IP 10.10.5.21.52344 > 3.120.45.9.443: Flags [P.], seq 2921:3120, ack 1, win 64240, length 199
12:01:05.500000 IP 10.10.5.21.52344 > 3.120.45.9.443: Flags [P.], seq 3120:4580, ack 1, win 64240, length 1460 (retransmission)
12:01:06.000000 IP 10.10.5.21.52344 > 3.120.45.9.443: Flags [R], seq 4580, win 0
```
We see multiple segments for the ClientHello (so a >1500B ClientHello), then retransmits, then RST from our side after timeout.

Devon (Eng-Infra): That tcpdump looks like the ClientHello is fragmented across multiple TCP segments. If your egress firewall or ISP is configured to drop IP fragments (or perform TLS inspection that only handles whole records), the server may never see a complete ClientHello and won't respond. For mTLS the ClientHello often includes SNI + large extension fields and can cross MTU. Two things to check immediately: 1) any TLS/SSL inspection / SSL Forward Proxy rules on the Palo Alto or ASA that target this FQDN? 2) any policy that drops "fragmented IP" or blocks TCP segments with DF/MSS interactions.

Marcus (Customer): We confirmed we do NOT have ssl-decrypt for that destination, but we do have a global "drop fragmented packets" rule enabled by our security team to reduce attack surface. We turned it on the same time as the outage.

Ingrid (SRE): That matches. If fragments are dropped, the control plane never receives the full ClientHello. Two quick mitigations you can try:
- enable MSS clamping / TCP MTU clamp on the egress NAT to 1300 (to ensure ClientHello fits a single segment)
- or disable the "drop fragmented packets" rule for traffic destined to cp.prod.redwood.example (preferred is allowlist to our control plane IP ranges)
Also please run `tcpdump -s 0 -w full.pcap host 3.120.45.9 and port 443` while reproducing so we can confirm the change.

Marcus (Customer): We applied MSS clamping to 1300 on the egress router and restarted the agent process. Re-ran the openssl command and agent. New output:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=cp.prod.redwood.example
   i:/CN=Redwood-Private-CA
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=cp.prod.redwood.example
issuer=/CN=Redwood-Private-CA
---
SSL handshake has read 3867 bytes and written 2785 bytes
---
Verify return code: 0 (ok)
```
Agent logs: `mTLS handshake completed: client cert verified, session established`

Sam (support): Great — can you confirm stability? Also please share the final tcpdump if possible so we attach to the ticket for internal docs.

Marcus (Customer): Confirmed. Handshake stable, no timeouts for 48h after the MSS change. Uploaded full.pcap.

Devon (Eng-Infra): Thanks. Action items: 1) We'll add a short KB note under Private/VPC onboarding: "If you see mTLS handshake timeouts to the control plane after firewall changes, check for MTU/fragmentation or TLS-inspection middleboxes. Recommend MSS clamping to 1300 or allowlisting control plane IPs and disabling TLS-inspection for that FQDN." 2) Sam, please close ticket after customer confirms 24h.

Sam (support): Adding KB draft and assigning to docs/devex. Marcus — glad it's resolved, leaving this open for 24h then closing. :thumbsup:

Marcus (Customer): Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick help. :tada:
